## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `occupancy-interval-contention-inference`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-08-01T09:51:18.539Z.

Catalog entry, by slug: occupancy-interval-contention-inference

Recorded 2026-08-01. Extends the catalog; no prior entry is renumbered or restated. Owner recorded on the algorithm portfolio registry (pm-g8t7b9). Filed alongside pm-1wujzi, which owns the missing read surface this entry consumes.

The gap this closes, stated against an entry that already exists. Entry (24), fleet-joint context diversification, conditions each agent's selection on what its peers already hold, and justifies the assumption in one sentence: "the claim ledger says who holds what ... readable without new distributed machinery." That sentence is half true and the false half is load-bearing. The ledger does say who holds what. Reading it is a fold over one item's entire history stream, performed by resolveClaimStateContext in the single-item get path and reachable from nowhere else, so approximating a peer set of P agents costs P stream folds, and asking the workspace-level question — which of N items is held — costs N. On this tracker that is 2,258 folds over 42,771 entries for one query. Entry (24) is correct as an objective and unimplementable as specified until occupancy is served from maintained state.

But the more interesting observation is that the fold discards more than it costs. It keeps the last claim and the last release. The stream holds every claim and every release, each with a timestamp and an author identity, which means occupancy is not a boolean at now — it is an interval-valued relation over the whole history, and the intervals are the signal.

The algorithm. Let S be the union of history streams. Project the subsequence of entries whose op is claim or release, each carrying (item, ts, actor), where actor is the agent instance when present and falls back to author identity. Fold per item into a sequence of occupancy intervals: a claim opens an interval, a matching release closes it, a claim while an interval is open closes the previous one as superseded, and an interval still open at head is live. Annotate each interval with whether any content-mutating op for that item falls strictly inside it — the ops are already distinguishable in the stream: update, comment_add, files_add, tests_add, docs_add, note_add, learning_add, append, close.

Reconstructed on this corpus today, which is what makes the entry adoptable rather than speculative: 2,109 productive intervals with mutation during hold, 25 intervals with a clean claim/release and no mutation between them, and 295 intervals superseded by a later claim without an intervening release. Zero live intervals at the moment of measurement, so the current-occupancy term is exercised only under load, while the historical terms are available immediately over the whole corpus.

Three signals fall out, and they are different questions that a single boolean cannot answer.

Live avoidance. The set of items with an open interval, with holder identity. This is entry (24)'s peer input, and once occupancy is maintained state rather than a per-item fold, it is a set membership test rather than a scan.

Contention prior. Occupancy density per item and, by projection through the typed graph, per neighbourhood: how often a region of the project has been held by more than one actor within a window. A region with a high contention prior is expensive to allocate into regardless of who holds it right now, which is information an allocator (pm-3oqjnc) needs before it has any live signal at all — on a cold fleet, live occupancy is empty and the prior is the only evidence available.

Abandonment. An interval with no mutation between claim and release is a recorded attempt that produced nothing. Twenty-five of them on this corpus is a small number and that is exactly why it is useful: abandonment is rare enough that each instance is a strong signal about the item rather than noise about the process. Ranked into an assembly, an abandoned attempt is high-value context for the next agent to approach the same work — someone tried this and stopped, and the stream says who and when, so the surrounding cohort of what they touched instead is recoverable through co-mutation-cohort-inference.

Hand-off continuity, which is the composition rather than a fourth signal. Two adjacent intervals on one item held by different actors form an implicit hand-off. For an agent resuming work, the previous holder's session cohort is a better seed set than the item's own graph neighbourhood, because it is what was actually in play when the work was last touched.

Cost and scale. The projection is a single ordered pass over the claim/release subsequence, which is a small fraction of entries — 5,026 of 42,771 here, under twelve percent. The fold is monotonic in stream length because the stream is append-only, so the result is cacheable keyed by (stream id, entry count, tail hash) with incremental extension, the same content-addressed discipline state-erased-signal-recovery and the attested-reads work already use, and the two should share one pass over history rather than each making their own. Live occupancy is a bounded set — at most one entry per concurrently held item — so serving it is O(held) rather than O(corpus), which is the property that makes the fleet question affordable at a million items. Historical density folds into a decayed summary past the retention horizon, so a decade of history costs what a month costs at lower resolution for the distant past.

Required degeneracies, which are the acceptance conditions and the falsifier.

On a single-agent workspace every interval has the same actor, so the contention prior is identically zero and live avoidance never fires. The small end must pay nothing: no ranking distortion, no measurable latency, and the assembly must be byte-identical to today.

On a workspace where claiming is not used at all — which is permitted, since claim is advisory — every term is identically zero and the engine behaves exactly as it does now. The algorithm must never manufacture occupancy from assignee, which is a mutable metadata field that survives release and is set on 288 items here without implying that any of them is held.

Abandonment must not be inferred from a short interval. A claim released in ninety seconds after a one-line correction is productive; a claim held for a day with no mutation is abandoned. The discriminator is mutation-during-hold, never duration, because duration measures the agent and mutation measures the work.

Contention must decay. An item contended six months ago and quiet since is not contended. Without decay the prior monotonically accumulates and eventually ranks the oldest items highest, which is the failure mode every recency-free signal in this catalog has been designed against.

The falsifier. Compute the contention prior over the corpus and correlate it against rework — items whose history shows a close followed by a reopening or a superseding item. If contention density carries no signal about rework, the prior is decorative and belongs behind a shape condition rather than in the default path. That test is cheap, runs entirely offline against recorded history, and needs no change to any write path to perform.

What this entry is not. It is not entry (24), which decides what each agent sees given a peer set; this supplies and extends the peer set. It is not pm-3oqjnc, which decides which agent works on which item; this supplies a prior it consumes. It is not co-mutation-cohort-inference, which infers association from mutation timing across items; this reads a declared, explicitly recorded relation between an actor and one item, and the two compose — cohorts explain what a holder was doing, intervals explain when they held it. It is not the usage-affinity signal, which learns from what was served. And it asserts nothing about whether claiming ought to be mandatory; it reads what was recorded and stays silent about what should have been.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
